Backbone horizontal, C=O up, acid at right, all methyl H shown - reproduces the source (p17 Checkpoint) well. Source additionally labels the two carbons C1/C2; ours is unlabelled (annotation only, not a structural difference).

discrepancies.aspect: Minor layout difference: source keeps OH to the left of the chiral C; our skeletal puts OH pointing down and C≡N up. Both are valid skeletal conventions.

discrepancies.aspect: The 'displayed' render is identical to the structural/skeletal (hexagon + inscribed circle + condensed CH3); it is not a true fully-displayed formula (no Kekulé bonds, no explicit C-H). discrepancies.aspect: Primary source (this PDF p24) draws CH3 to the side (horizontal), which our render reproduces exactly. (Secondary Arene refs place CH3 at the top vertex, but the primary source form matches.)

discrepancies.fix: No change needed; Br to the side and upright roman both match the primary source.

discrepancies.aspect: 1-chloro-4-methylcyclohexane is ACHIRAL. Its only stereoisomers are cis/trans diastereomers, and both are superimposable on their own mirror images (RDKit-confirmed: 2 stereoisomers, each achiral). The render marks it chiral and labels the pair 'enantiomers / non-superimposable mirror images', which is chemically false.
discrepancies.fix: Suppress enantiomer generation when every stereoisomer of a symmetric 1,4-disubstituted ring is achiral; if configuration must be shown, draw cis vs trans on the ring, not enantiomers.

discrepancies.aspect: The stereo panel is visually broken: the right-hand enantiomer has a long bond slashing through the 'CH2CH2CH(Cl)CH2CH2' label and 'CH3' overprinting the ring chain, making it unreadable. The ring is drawn as two duplicated open condensed chains, so it reads as an acyclic di-chloro species rather than one ring bearing a single Cl.
discrepancies.fix: Render cyclic stereocentres on an actual ring skeleton using wedge/dash to the substituents; never open the ring into duplicated condensed chains, and resolve the label/bond collisions.

discrepancies.aspect: Skeletal/structural/displayed correctly reproduce the source p27 Q1(c): plain hexagon (no circle), Cl on the left and CH3 on the right in a 1,4 (para) arrangement. Only nit: Cl is upright roman, whereas the NJC source italicises the l (Cl).
discrepancies.fix: Italicise the halogen letter to match house style; the ring/substitution pattern is correct.

discrepancies.aspect: Source p28 Q4(e) draws the acetyl group with an explicit carbonyl C=O pointing UP (ring-C(=O)-CH3). Our skeletal (and structural/displayed) condense it to a '-COCH3' label with no drawn C=O, failing both the source drawing and the house 'C=O points up' convention.
discrepancies.fix: Draw the ketone carbonyl explicitly as a ring-attached vertex with a double bond to O pointing up, then CH3, instead of the condensed COCH3 label.

discrepancies.aspect: Chirality classification is correct here (C1 is a genuine stereocentre), but the stereo panel is visually broken: the right enantiomer's bond slashes through the 'CH2CH=CHCH=CH' and 'COCH3' labels which overprint one another. The ring is opened into two duplicated condensed diene chains, reading as an acyclic species rather than a cyclohexa-2,4-diene ring.
discrepancies.fix: Draw the stereocentre on the real cyclohexadiene ring with wedge/dash to H and the acetyl group; keep the C=O explicit and fix label/bond overlaps.

discrepancies.aspect: Ring connectivity (two conjugated ring C=C, sp3 substituted carbon) matches the source; only the carbonyl depiction is the issue.
discrepancies.fix: No change needed for the ring itself.

discrepancies.aspect: Matches source p28 Q4(f): plain hexagon (no circle) with -Cl on the right vertex; our render reproduces this in all three forms. Only nit: source italicises the l (Cl); our Cl is upright roman.
discrepancies.fix: Italicise the halogen letter to match house style.

discrepancies.aspect: cis geometry only loosely conveyed: our render lays both Cl collinear with the C=C axis (Cl-C=C-Cl flat) and both H straight up, so bond angles are ~90 degrees rather than trigonal and the geometry is ambiguous. NJC (p2) draws both Cl on ~120-degree splayed bonds at the TOP (same side) with both H at the bottom.

discrepancies.aspect: Cl set with an upright 'l'; NJC house style typesets it with an italic lowercase l (C + italic l).

discrepancies.aspect: Does NOT show trans. The displayed pane is geometrically identical to our cis-1,2-dichloroethene render (Cl-C=C-Cl flat, both H up), so it reads as cis and a viewer cannot tell the two isomers apart. NJC (p2) draws Cl up-left and Cl down-right (opposite corners).

discrepancies.aspect: Does NOT show trans. The displayed pane is identical to our cis-but-2-ene render (flat CH3-CH=CH-CH3, both vinyl H up), so it reads as cis. NJC (p4) draws H3C and CH3 on OPPOSITE sides of the C=C.

discrepancies.aspect: Convention: source uses condensed H3C / CH3 labels; ours fully displays every methyl H.

discrepancies.aspect: The '+' charge is omitted in the skeletal pane (plain 2-carbon line to Br), so it reads as neutral bromoethane rather than a carbocation.

discrepancies.aspect: Convention differs from NJC p11: the source draws the reacting C=C as a splayed trigonal group with a CONDENSED CH2CH3 substituent (mixed displayed/condensed); our render fully displays the whole chain and draws the C=C flat and in-line. discrepancies.aspect: Source (p11) uses a condensed CH2CH3 tail; ours fully displays every carbon and H. Correct 1-bromobutane (Br on terminal carbon), different convention only.

discrepancies.aspect: Displayed pane correctly shows the 2-degree cation (CH+ with two alkyl groups and one H). Source (p11/p12) condenses the ethyl to CH2CH3 and places '+' beside C; ours fully displays and uses a superscript C+.

discrepancies.aspect: Wedge/hash assignments are swapped relative to NJC p12 (source: Br hashed/back, H bold-wedge/forward; ours: Br bold-wedge/forward, H hashed/back). discrepancies.aspect: Orientation differs: source draws a pointy-top hexagon with the methyl pointing straight UP from the apex and the C=C on the upper-right edge; our render is a flat-top hexagon with the methyl pointing horizontally right and the C=C on the lower-right edge. discrepancies.aspect: Our 'displayed' and 'structural' panels are identical to the skeletal drawing (no C-H bonds shown). Source only used the skeletal form here, so not critical, but the displayed form is not truly displayed.

discrepancies.aspect: Chemically correct but different layout from source. Source draws a 2D-splayed structure: (CH3)(CH3)C=C(CH2CH3)(H) with the two methyls, the ethyl and the H on splayed bonds around a displayed C=C. Our render is a linear condensed formula CH3-C(=CH-CH2-CH3) with the 2-methyl written above C2.

discrepancies.aspect: Both are correct displayed forms but oriented differently. Our render puts the two OH at the horizontal chain ends with explicit O-H bonds (H-O-CH2-CH2-O-H), H atoms up/down on the carbons.

discrepancies.aspect: Constitutional-isomer mismatch. The source draws the methyl on an sp2 (double-bond) carbon (a 1-methylcyclopenta-1,3-diene): the ring's sp3 CH2 is the apex and the methyl-bearing carbon is part of a C=C. This is confirmed by the drawn cold-KMnO4 tetraol product, whose methyl-bearing carbon carries an OH. Our SMILES CC1C=CC=C1 places the methyl on the sp3 CH carbon with both C=C on the far edges, so the render depicts a different isomer than the notes.
discrepancies.fix: Use a SMILES with the methyl on a double-bond carbon, e.g. CC1=CC=CC1 (1-methylcyclopenta-1,3-diene), to match the source substrate.

discrepancies.aspect: displayed/structural panels are identical to the skeletal (ring H atoms not shown), and carry the same isomer error.

discrepancies.aspect: Connectivity matches source (cyclohexene C=C on the substituent-bearing edge, CH2-COOH chain off C1). Notation differs slightly: source writes the side chain as 'CH2COOH'; our render writes 'CH2C(=O)OH' (carbonyl made explicit).

discrepancies.aspect: structural/displayed panels are identical to the skeletal (ring C-H bonds not shown). Source used skeletal only, so not critical.

discrepancies.aspect: Structure is broken: the fused bicyclic gamma-lactone is NOT drawn. discrepancies.aspect: The stereo pair is garbled and illegible: two overlapping condensed strings (CH2C(=O)OCHCH2CH2CH2CH2 / CH(OC(=O)CH2)CH2CH2CH2CH2CHOC(=O)CH2) with scattered stray wedge/dash marks and a floating I. It does not depict the iodolactone or a valid enantiomer pair.

discrepancies.aspect: Same open-chain, ring-not-closed, iodine-missing errors as the skeletal form.

discrepancies.aspect: Pent-2-ene is not drawn at the cited reference. The referenced Q7b is a distinguishing-test question showing two DIFFERENT 4-carbon alkenes to be told apart, not cis/trans of one compound. Exact vector coordinates confirm each drawn chain has only 4 carbons: the left structure is but-1-ene (terminal C=C, CH2=CH-CH2-CH3) and the right is trans-but-2-ene (internal C=C, CH3-CH=CH-CH3). Our render draws pent-2-ene (5 carbons), which is correct for the given name/SMILES but does not appear in the source. The manifest ref/notes misidentify these Q7b structures.
discrepancies.fix: Re-map this compound: the source location depicts but-1-ene and but-2-ene, not pent-2-ene; either correct the reference or drop this compound from the alkene set.

discrepancies.aspect: Terminal hydroxyl drawn as an explicit O-H bond (H-C-C-O-H) whereas Ch23 p1 draws it as a grouped 'OH' (H-C-C-OH). Chemically equivalent and the explicit O-H matches the p5 mechanism drawing, so acceptable; for an exact p1 match, render the terminal as a single '-OH' group.

discrepancies.aspect: Condensed CH3-CH2-OH is correct A-level structural notation but is not the form the source used (source used the displayed comb layout); no error, just noting the source drew displayed.

discrepancies.aspect: Source (p2) writes 'COOH' as a condensed label above the top vertex of a hexagon+circle; our render is faithful in ring type and label spelling (COOH matches p2, not CO2H). Only difference is the substituent sits to the right instead of on top.

discrepancies.aspect: All three columns are identical text-label renders; the displayed column keeps 'COOH' rather than breaking out the carbonyl. Acceptable since p2 also uses the condensed label, but it is not a true displayed carboxyl.

discrepancies.aspect: Substituent placed to the right vs source's top-vertex placement; all three columns are identical. Condensed 'CHO' is a valid depiction (matches the secondary 7 Arenes convention) but not the primary source's look.

discrepancies.aspect: Faithful: hexagon+circle with condensed 'NO2' (subscript 2), charges not drawn, matching p2/memory-sheet convention. Substituent is to the right rather than on the top vertex.

per_form_quality.assessment: Generally faithful for connectivity and condensed labels (matches source in the majority of arenes and chains). Chief weakness is that it is rarely a genuinely distinct form: it usually clones the skeletal render (hexagon + inscribed circle), and it occasionally garbles condensed groups (triiodomethyl 'CI3' printed as 'Cl3', cramped 'C-Cl'). Reliable for connectivity, weak as an independent representation.

Conceptually the weakest 2-D form and the highest-impact target. Frequently NOT truly displayed: collapses carbonyls/esters/vinyl/CHO to condensed text, reuses the skeletal hexagon+circle, and critically fails E/Z so cis and trans look identical. When it does draw every atom (ethane, ethene, ethyne, bromoethane, ethanoic acid) it matches the notes well.

The strongest and most dependable form. Zig-zags, C=C placement, and the plain-hexagon (aliphatic) vs hexagon+circle (aromatic) distinction are consistently correct, and it correctly encodes E/Z where the displayed form does not. Weaknesses: omits '+' charges on carbocations (reads as neutral), fails to close fused rings, and differs in flat-top vs pointy-top orientation.

The most broken form. Works for simple acyclic single-stereocentre cases (lactic acid, 2-bromobutane, alanine), but for rings and multi-stereocentre molecules it opens rings into overlapping condensed chains, lets wedge/dash bonds slash through atom labels (illegible), and emits enantiomer pairs even for achiral molecules or with the wrong stereocentre count. Needs the most engineering.

systematic_issues.issue: Displayed form collapses functional groups/carbonyls to inline condensed text instead of drawing explicit atoms and bonds, so a 'displayed formula' hides the very atoms it should show (amide, ester, aldehyde CHO, vinyl, acetyl COCH3); in the worst case a triiodomethyl carbon collapses to a chloride-like 'Cl3' and vanillin's methoxy drops its methyl to a dangling '-O'.
systematic_issues.fix: In displayed mode expand every functional group to explicit atoms/bonds: draw C=O as a vertical (up) double bond, aldehyde as O=C-H, ester as -O-C(=O)-, vinyl as H2C=CH; render the triiodomethyl carbon as an explicit C bonded to three capital-I iodines (never 'Cl3'), and never drop a substituent atom (methoxy = O-CH3).

systematic_issues.issue: Fused and substituted rings are not closed: the engine opens the ring into duplicated dangling condensed chains and drops substituents, so decalin, indan-1-one and the iodolactone render as an open hexagon with pendant CH2 strings (iodine missing entirely).
systematic_issues.fix: Implement proper ring perception and closure so all rings, including fused/bridged bicyclics, render as closed polygons sharing the fusion edge with substituents kept on the correct ring carbon; never linearise a ring into condensed text as a fallback.

systematic_issues.issue: Stereo/enantiomer panels are illegible and sometimes chemically false: condensed labels overlap, wedge/dash bonds slash through atom text, and enantiomer pairs are generated even for achiral molecules (1-chloro-4-methylcyclohexane) or where the drawn atom is not a stereocentre / the stereocentre count is misrepresented.
systematic_issues.fix: In stereo mode draw the parent skeleton exactly once, place a single wedge+dash pair only on genuine stereocentres, run an RDKit chirality/symmetry check to suppress enantiomer pairs when every stereoisomer is achiral (draw cis/trans instead) or the stereocentre count is wrong, and add collision avoidance so bonds never cross atom labels.

systematic_issues.issue: Manifest data errors upstream of the renderer: a SMILES encodes the wrong constitutional isomer (3-chlorocyclohexanol drawn as the 4-chloro/para isomer; cyclopentadiene methyl on the wrong carbon), a name disagrees with its structure (2-bromobutan-1-ol is really 3-bromo), or the compound is absent from the cited source (pent-2-ene, 2-methylprop-1-ene).
systematic_issues.fix: Add a pre-render validation step reconciling each manifest SMILES with its IUPAC name and the cited source figure (RDKit canonicalisation + locant check): correct 3-chlorocyclohexanol to OC1CC(Cl)CCC1, fix the cyclopentadiene methyl position, rename 2-bromobutan-1-ol, and drop or remap compounds not actually drawn in the source.

systematic_issues.issue: E/Z geometry is lost in the displayed form: cis and trans isomers render identically (both Cl or both CH3 laid collinear with the C=C), so a viewer cannot tell the two isomers apart.
systematic_issues.fix: Honour the SMILES double-bond stereo in the displayed layout by placing like substituents on the same side (cis) or opposite sides (trans) on ~120-degree trigonal bonds; the skeletal pane already encodes E/Z correctly and can be used as the geometry reference.

systematic_issues.issue: The three forms are not differentiated: displayed and structural panels are byte-identical to the skeletal render (typically a bare hexagon + inscribed circle or bare pentagon), so the 'displayed' form shows no explicit atoms or bonds and a circle is not a valid displayed formula.
systematic_issues.fix: Generate a genuinely distinct displayed formula (Kekule ring with every C-H for arenes, expanded CH2/CH for saturated rings) rather than cloning the skeletal drawing; reserve the inscribed circle for the aromatic skeletal form only.

systematic_issues.issue: Formal charges are omitted or misplaced, especially in the skeletal pane: carbocations lose the '+' and read as neutral alkanes, and the cyanate '-' sits on the wrong terminal atom.
systematic_issues.fix: Propagate formal charges to every form so carbocations show '+' in skeletal, place the cyanate '-' on the correct terminal atom, and render the anionic minus as the notes' circled minus.

systematic_issues.issue: Resonance sets and side-by-side paired figures render as a single structure: the ethanoate resonance pair, the ortho/para '&' halophenol pair, and the but-2-ene/but-1-ene pair each lose their second structure.
systematic_issues.fix: When a manifest entry denotes a resonance set or a paired figure, emit all contributors linked by a double-headed arrow (ethanoate) or both molecules joined by '&' (2-/4-halophenol), and render companion isomers alongside (but-1-ene with but-2-ene).

systematic_issues.issue: Benzene-ring orientation differs from the notes: the principal substituent sits on a side vertex rather than the top vertex, para/ortho pairs are drawn horizontally instead of vertically, and hexagons are flat-top where the house default is pointy-top.
systematic_issues.fix: Default arene rings to pointy-top (vertex-up) with the principal substituent on the top vertex and para/ortho pairs oriented vertically, to match the house layout.

systematic_issues.issue: Chlorine's 'l' is typeset as an upright roman letter instead of the house italic lowercase l.
systematic_issues.fix: Typeset the halogen letter in Cl with an italic lowercase l to match NJC house typography.

systematic_issues.issue: Carboxyl spelling does not track the specific source figure: 'COOH' is used where that exact figure writes 'CO2H' (and vice versa).
systematic_issues.fix: Carry the exact acid spelling (COOH vs CO2H) from the source figure per compound rather than applying a single global default.

r2_rerun.method: Replayed every affected rule through the renderer and the repository test gate. The source PDFs and a visual adjudicator are not stored in this repository, so this is a rule-level rerun, not a new pixel or vision score.
